title: Transition to long-playing records and sorting the Period albums
summary: Hughes and Maxine try to straighten out the three Period LPs and the Jazztone reissue.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: So what we've covered up to now then, is your entire recording history during the 78 rpm era.
And the next sessions you made were
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
explicitly designed to be released on long playing records. And these would be the first long playing records.
So we've come to a kind of transition in your recording career.
Yes. Well also, in the industry itself.
For sure.
Yeah.
Are we talking about the Period records -- the Period albums?
Yes, they're the next ones.
What we're saying is --
We're back on tape now after taking about half an hour to try and sort through the rather scruffy information concerning your 1955 and 1956 LP recording sessions.
Yeah.
These records appeared under a number of different labels. There are three period LP's listed in the discography.
A selection from them came out on
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
Jazztone, which is a record that you have in your collection. We've seen that one. And you also have one of the Period albums which is Period SLPl207. Excuse me, SPL.
It says here SLO.
That's incorrect. We have the album here. We have Period SPL1207 which is a musical tribute to the lyrics of Andy Razaf. But the other material, we don't have, and it's a little bit confusing.
I'm --
What do you remember about it?
I'm going to try to clarify some of this jamble.
The one album that's listed, it has "Flow Gently Sweet Rhythm" in it. It came out, I think as Flow Gently Sweet Rhythm, but it was --
On the Period label --
On the Period label. And I, at the time that they made this album, I recorded two selections: "Molly Malone" and "If I Had A Ribbon
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
Bow."
The purpose of this album was to more or less revive the memory of the show that Kirby and I had called "Flow Gently Sweet Rhythm."
Yeah, which you talked about last time.
Right.
And Leonard was able to assemble those musicians who were still living of the original John Kirby Orchestra. And it was more or less considered a reunion.
Everything except the bass and drums.
Yeah.
We had to replace Kirby, of course, who had gone by that time. And O'Neil Spencer, who was no longer with us.

But that album at the time it was recorded, was intended more or less to be more instrumental, not necessarily a Maxine Sullivan presentation. I just appeared as a guest, and "Molly Malone" and "If I Had A Ribbon Bow" were two of my
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
big numbers that I had going for me at the time.
I wondered if that wasn't a 10-inch LP.
No, it wasn't a 10-inch LP.
